bibliographic.title: Head-to-Tail: How Knowledgeable are Large Language Models (LLMs)? A.K.A. Will LLMs Replace Knowledge Graphs?
bibliographic.authors: Kai Sun, Yifan Ethan Xu, Hanwen Zha, Yue Liu, Xin Luna Dong
bibliographic.citation_apa: Sun, K., Xu, Y. E., Zha, H., Liu, Y., & Dong, X. L. (2023). Head-to-Tail: How knowledgeable are large language models (LLMs)? A.K.A. Will LLMs replace knowledge graphs? arXiv preprint arXiv:2308.10168.

methodology.method_family: benchmark construction and automated LLM evaluation
methodology.study_design: comparative benchmark evaluation using question-answer accuracy metrics across head, torso, and tail entity popularity strata
methodology.sample_description: 18K question-answer pairs in the Head-to-Tail benchmark; evaluation of 16 publicly available LLMs including GPT-4, ChatGPT, and Llama 2
methodology.technology_context: factual knowledge assessment of LLMs; comparison with knowledge graphs; hallucination and factuality

eligibility.exclusion_reason: Empirical benchmark study on LLM factual knowledge and knowledge graph replacement; does not address conversational governance, oversight, compliance, audit, or regulated deployment contexts.
eligibility.decision_rationale: The paper constructs Head-to-Tail, an 18K QA benchmark, and evaluates 16 LLMs on factual knowledge across head/torso/tail entities. Although it mentions hallucinations, factuality, and briefly discusses explainability in a knowledge-graph architecture proposal, it does not study conversational systems governance, human oversight, accountability, monitoring, compliance, or regulated-sector deployment. Python triage hits for chatbot, law, logs, and explainability are weak or misleading relative to review scope.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Scope mismatch is clear from title, abstract, and introduction; no governance or regulated-environment focus evident in supplied text.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal based on limited supplied excerpts (mainly page 1 and fragments). Objective and benchmark-oriented method appear clearly stated; ethics, full sampling details, and complete results not visible in provided text.

cerqual.explanation: Internally coherent empirical benchmark study with a clear research question, but low relevance to conversational governance in regulated LLM systems based on available text.

coding.subtheme: benchmarking knowledge depth versus knowledge graphs

synthesis.main_claim: Existing LLMs remain far from perfect in grasping factual knowledge, especially for torso-to-tail entities; LLM QA accuracy is used as a proxy for internalized knowledge.
synthesis.contribution: Introduces Head-to-Tail, an 18K QA benchmark with automated metrics evaluating 16 public LLMs, and frames whether LLMs can replace knowledge graphs.
synthesis.limitations: Provided text notes difficulty directly querying embedded LLM knowledge and that hallucination may stem from lack of knowledge or generative dysfunction; fuller limitations not visible in excerpt.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude as central or supporting evidence for conversational governance in regulated LLM systems; at most marginal foundational context on hallucination and factuality risks.
